To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated a universal wet‐chemial shell‐by‐shel coating procedure for the preparation of colloidal metal oxide nanoparticles with dynamically and reversible tunable surface energies, and that this covalent functionalisation sequence is extended towards noncovalent attachments of tailor‐made amphiphilic surfactants.
we have developed a novel universal wet‐chemical method to prepare colloidal nanoparticles with tunable surface energies in three orthogonal solvents.

we have developed a universal coating procedure that enables the orthogonal adjustment of surface energies in three different media (water, hydrocarbons and fluorocarbons) and thus, the reversible control of the colloidal stability in each of these three media.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new concept for the synthesis of colloidal metal oxide nanoparticles with orthogonally adjustable dispersibility in hydrocarbons, fluoro‐, and water phases.
the development and application of new nanoscale materials.
the design and synthesis of colloidal nanoparticles with tunable surface properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the combination of covalent and solvophobic surface modification of nanoparticles allows for the design and preparation of colloids that are dispersible in all three states of matter, i.e. in water, hydrocarbons as well as fluorocarbons.
the presented approach allows to manufacture nanoparticles with orthogonally adjustable dispersibility in hydrocarbons, fluorocarbons and water.
the presented coating strategy provides a universal approach for the preparation of nanoparticles with tunable colloidal properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the combination of covalent and noncovalent surface functionalizations of metal oxide nanoparticles allows for the synthesis of a broad variety of nanoparticles with orthogonal and tunable surface properties, which can be used as model systems for fundamental research and for the development of new functional materials.
we are able to manufacture nanoparticles with orthogonally tunable dispersibility in fluorocarbon, hydrocarbons and water.
the combination of a covalent and a noncovalent surface functionalisation allows for a universal and orthogonal coating procedure to tune the surface energies of metal oxide nanoparticles.
The main takeaway from our work is that

this approach can be extended to a variety of other metal oxide nanoparticles and other noncovalent amphiphiles, which can be used to tailor the dispersibility of the metal oxide core in a broad range of solvents and solutes.

we have demonstrated that the surface energies of colloidal metal oxide nanoparticles can be dynamically and reversibly adjusted via a simple, universal coating procedure, and that this approach can be applied to other nanoparticles and other solvents.
this approach allows us to tune the dispersibility of the nanoparticles in any solvent, and thus, to create nanoparticles that are soluble in all of the major classes of solvents.
